chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani, who said, and he was with us, performing pilgrimage. He said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) on the hands of my father: May I be sacrificed for you, our companions have disputed regarding the sa'. Some of them say that the Fitra is [given by] a sa' of Medina, and some of them say [by] a sa' of Iraq. Then he wrote to me: A sa' is six artals by the Medinan standard, and nine artals by the Iraqi standard. He said: He also informed me and said: By weight, it is one thousand and one hundred and seventy weights.

key_terms.أَرْطَال: Artal, a unit of weight (pound) used in the measurement of the sa'.
key_terms.الصَّاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods, used here for Zakat al-Fitr.
key_terms.الْعِرَاقِيِّ: The standard of Iraq, referring to the specific measurement system used in Iraq.
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory alms tax given at the end of Ramadan.
key_terms.الْمَدِينِيِّ: The standard of Medina, referring to the specific measurement system used in Medina.

ai.seo_question: What is the weight and measurement of the sa' for Zakat al-Fitr according to Imam al-Hassan (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* resolves the juristic dispute regarding the volume of the 'sa'' used for Zakat al-Fitr by providing precise metrological conversions between the Medinan and Iraqi standards. It establishes that while the volume differs, the weight equivalence (1,170 units) ensures consistency in charitable obligations, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on reconciling regional variations with divine command. This clarification underscores the practical application of Quranic injunctions on purification through tangible, measurable acts of charity.
